summary: A follows the frozen contract’s required architecture: it uses multipartbody.NewFile and delegates to FilesService.Add. B adds broader retry machinery and duplicates Add instead of routing through it, both explicitly contrary to the contract.
reasons: A preserves Add unchanged and implements Upload as a thin convenience wrapper around it.
A uses the required multipart field "file", passes the supplied filename, buffers via the established multipartbody helper, and propagates helper/reader errors.

B reimplements FilesService.Add’s option handling, request execution, response decoding, and missing-data error path inside Upload, violating the requirement to keep those semantics centralized in Add.

B changes RawClient retry behavior for every seekable request body and documents changed Add/Update semantics, despite the contract explicitly forbidding unrelated request/retry refactoring and requiring FilesOption behavior to remain centralized through Add delegation.
risks_a: The tests do not explicitly cover empty-filename validation, nil content, or source-reader failures.
The retry test does not set RetryAllMethods explicitly and only verifies the call count, not that multipart content is intact on every attempt.
The combined validation error is less precise than separate filename/content errors, though it still satisfies pre-request validation.
risks_b: Upload bypasses Add, so future fixes or semantic changes to Add can diverge from Upload.
The global seekable-reader replay mechanism expands behavior beyond the requested API and introduces shared-reader ownership and potential concurrency concerns.
No test covers source-reader failures, despite that being part of the requested verification.
